Recommendations/observations  
 
14. The Committee notes that NYKS implements and also h as to undertake a number of 
important programmes mentioned above.  However, due  to inadequate funds which work out to 
about Rs.8 lakhs per District only, NYKS will not b e able to cater to a small fraction of the youth 
enrolled with its Youth Clubs.  Most of it goes in paying salaries and allowances only.  Further, 
regarding five parameters falling under NYKS, viz. No. of volunteers enrolled, Skill Upgradation 
Training Programme, Promotion of Sports (sports mat erials to youth clubs), National Integration 
Camps and Tribal Youth Exchange; the Committee find s that there are no substantial short-falls in 
the targets fixed and the achievements made. The Co mmittee, accordingly recommends need to 
increase the funding for NYKS for taking up its var ious programmes. The matter should be taken 
up at RE stage for additional fund allocation for N YKS.  In addition, efforts be made for 
mobilization of funds for NYKS from other Ministrie s/ Departments/ Organisations for taking up 
various programmes like 'Swachh Bharat', 'Beti Bach ao, Beti Padhao Aandolan', 'Aadarsh Gram 
Yojana', etc. The Department should also request th e State Governments to support NYKS by 
pooling their resources for its various schemes in view of devolution of funds to the States after 
14 th  Finance Commission's recommendations. 
 
Action Taken  
 
 In view of urgency of funds requirement for ongoin g programmes of NYKS, an additional 
allocation of Rs.25 crores (under Plan) has been ma de for NYKS at first supplementary stage, 
through internal appropriation within existing over all budget allocation. The necessary approval 
from Ministry of Finance has been received. Further  increase in allocations will be proposed at RE 
stage as per the funds requirement. NYKS has been m aking proactive efforts for mobilisation of 
funds from Central/ State Government Ministries/ De partments, other Organisations, etc. For 
instance, proposal has been sent to Ministry of Hom e Affairs for organising 8 th  Tribal Youth 
Exchange Programme involving 2,000 tribal youth fro m LWE-affected Districts and funds 
allocation is expected shortly. Similarly, the Mini stry of Social Justice and Empowerment, 
Government of India, has sanctioned Rs. 6.18 crore for two projects on Awareness and Education 
for Prevention of Drug Abuse and Alcoholism in 21 d istricts of Punjab, the implementation of 
which is going on . Further, NYKS is collaborating with United Nations Population Fund 
(UNFPA) for implementation of Adolescent Health and  Development Project in 10 Districts of 5 
states (viz. Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Od isha and Rajasthan) through 1,860 teen clubs. 
The total project cost is Rs. 3.43 crore for the year 2015. 
 
Regarding flagship initiatives of the Government su ch as 'Swachh Bharat', 'Beti Bachao Beti 
Padhao Aandolan', 'Aadarsh Gram Yojana', ‘Jan Dhan Yojana’, ‘Social Security Schemes’, etc., 
NYKS is working in close collaboration with Central  Ministries/ State Government Departments 
and local bodies for making these programmes a gran d success. NYKS has also signed an MOU 
with National Mission for Clean Ganga for implement ing a Project called ‘Youth Partnership in 
Ganga Rejuvenation Mission’ to create awareness in 1,649 Gram Panchayats along flanks of 

Ganga river for keeping the river clean.  Proactive  efforts are being made for pursing the matter 
with State Governments for supporting NYKS by pooli ng their resources for its various schemes. 
NYKS has also submitted a proposal for Rs. 1.72 cro re to Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment, Government of India, for celebration o f 125 th  birth Anniversary of Dr. B. R. 
Ambedkar. Under this Project, 105 Districts (36 Sta te Capitals/ UT HQs. and 69 other Districts) 
would be covered. In these Districts, it has been p roposed to organize activities such as Sports 
Tournaments, District Youth Conventions, Exhibition s, Casteless Youth Run/ Rallies/ Human 
Chain for National Unity, etc.  
 
Recommendations/observations  
15 . On a specific query regarding vacancies in NYKS, the Committee came to know that as per 
DOPT instructions, cadre restructuring needs to be undertaken every 5 years.  However, the same 
has not been done in case of NYKS.  The Committee f eels that the current structure is flawed, 
resulting in serious stagnation in promotions which  poses some operational difficulties.  The 
Committee, accordingly, recommends that it is imper ative to take urgent initiatives to fill-up 
vacant posts in NYKS, especially in the category of  District Youth Coordinators (DYCs) (342 
vacancies) and Accounts-cum-Typists (ACTs) (210 vac ancies).  These vacancies are adversely

Recommendations/observations  
53. As regards augmentation of funds concerning differe nt schemes of the Department, the

Action Taken  
 
 The Department has only one Scheme, namely, Nation al Service Scheme (NSS), where 
expenditure is shared between the Centre and the States, in the following ratio: 
 
a. In case of J&K and UTs (without legislature), the C entral Government provides 100%

crore (under Plan) has been made for NPYAD, through  internal appropriation within existing 
overall budget allocation of the Department. Proact ive efforts will be made at RE stage for further 
increase in the allocation for NPYAD, so that the P rogramme can be implemented smoothly and 
the intended objectives of this Programme can be achieved. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 The Committee is of the view that it would be appr eciated if concerted efforts bring 
the result concerning fund allocation for NPYAD. On  account of scarcity of requisite funds, 
the intended role of an umbrella programme for assi stance to various organizations 
concerning youth and development activities cannot be played by NPYAD.  Whether there 
has been an increase in the fund allocation at RE s tage cannot be ascertained as the Ministry 
of Finance is yet to give its acceptance to the budget proposal sent by the Department. 
 
RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF YOUTH DEVELOPMENT (RGNIYD)  
 
Recommendations/observations  
33. The Committee is constrained to note that the Budge t provision for BE 2015-16 has been 
kept at Rs. 20.00 crore (inclusive of Rs.2 crore fo r NE), as there is no increase in the overall 
Budget allocation for the Department in 2015-16, wh ich is kept at the same level as during 2014-
15, i.e., Rs. 384.00 crore.  The Committee is surpr ised that the decrease in budget allocation for 

this scheme in RE 2014-15 amounting to Rs.15.86  cr ore  with respect to Rs.20.00 crore in BE 
2014-15 is on account of Non-submission of Utilization Certificate, it is unacceptable.

 During current year, the timely release and utilis ation of funds is being closely monitored, 
so that allocated funds are fully utilised and fund s do not lapse on account of non-submission of 
UCs etc.

activities in rural, urban and also tribal areas. However, to note that the budget provision for

very unfortunate situation. The Committee finds the  response of the Department very 
routine. The Committee would like to reiterate that  concerted and serious efforts need to be 
taken up for the proper and full utilisation of fun ds and also ensure timely submission of 
Utilisation Certificates.

follow-up for increasing allocations for RGNIYD. Th e Committee strongly recommends for 
initiating requisite initiatives so as to curb the delay in getting U.Cs which hampers further 
budgetary allocations.  As regards the need for str engthening the faculty position of the Institute, 
the Committee is not fully convinced with the expla nation of the department.  In order to 
strengthen the faculty of the Institute, the Commit tee feels the academic posts have to be filled 
with a sense of urgency.

allocations at RE stage. Efforts are being made to expedite completion of the recruitment process 
for the existing vacant posts. The matter will be f ollowed up vigorously for sanction of additional 
posts as per the requirement of the Institute.

 Merely agreeing in principle by the Department to take up proactive efforts to utilise 
funds expeditiously and to expedite completion of t he recruitment process for the vacant 
posts, the Committee feels, are not enough. Urgent steps need to be taken up to complete the 
recruitment process. The Committee finds that the A ction Taken Notes submitted by the 
Government appears to be of routine nature and with out any determination for execution 

within a targeted time. The Committee once again em phasizes that the Department will have 
to make vigorous efforts to raise the required fund s for RGNIYD.  The Department could 
not give an exact amount of funds allocated at the RE stage as the budget proposals sent by 
the Department are yet to be accepted by the Ministry of Finance.

maintenance and operation of the Hostels.  The Stat e Governments do not sanction adequate funds

fact, 16 Youth Hostel buildings are under unauthori zed occupation and are being utilized for 
purposes other that the purpose for which these wer e constructed. In a number of cases, the Hostel

Department must take all appropriate steps to get 1 6 hostels vacated from unauthorized occupants

unauthorized occupancy of Youth Hostels will contin ue ceaselessly. The Committee, 
henceforth,  notes with dismay that inadequacy of r eal spirit would fail to promptly resolve 
the issue of unauthorized occupancy of Youth Hostels.

43. The Committee is also seized of the fact that the S tates have been demanding sanction of 
additional Hostels.  However, currently no new Host els are being set up.  The erstwhile Planning

 In the meeting of the Central Policy Committee hel d on 11.07.2015, it was decided that the

Committee feels that the Department should follow-up with NITI Ayog earnestly.

Resource Development deals with the action taken by  the Government on the recommendations 
contained in its Two hundred sixty-ninth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants 
(Demand No. 109) of the Ministry of Youth Affairs a nd Sports, Department of Sports, for the year 
2015-16.

CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
GOVERNMENT  
 
Recommendations/observations  
12. In view of the winding up of the Planning Commissio n, which was an in intermediary 
agency between the Centre and the States, and also acted as monitoring agency, it is not clear what 
monitoring mechanism of the centrally sponsored or central sector schemes would be put in place. 
 The Committee shows its concern and desires the De partment to clarify this issue before it at the 
earliest. 
 
Action Taken  
Grants released to State Governments/UTs, Non-Gover nmental Organizations (NGOs), 
National Sports Federations (NSFs) by the Ministry under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes or 
Central Sector Schemes are released keeping in view  provisions of the General Financial Rules. 
Grantees are required to submit audited statement o f accounts and the utilization certificate in the 
prescribed format and the same are duly scrutinized  in the Ministry to ensure that the funds have 
been utilized in accordance with the provisions of the sanction order and have been utilized for the 
purpose for which the grants were released. Further , there is audit by the Comptroller & Auditor 
General.  
 
SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA (SAI)  
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
17.  The Committee notes that although of late there has  been slight improvement in the 
performance of India’s sportspersons at internation al events but it is incomparable with the 
performance of other developing/developed nations f or which a lot needs to be done.  The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that SAI should co me up with more concerted efforts so as to 
increase its medals tally substantially during Olym pic Games, 2016.  Improvement of nation’s 
performance in sports is the need of the time as it  would not only bring national pride and glory 
but also instills some of confidence amongst the people. 
 
Action Taken  
Based on present standard of the Indian sportsperso ns/teams, priority areas are being 
identified and maximum thrust is being given to tho se disciplines/events where Indian 
sportspersons stand a chance to win a medal or at l east give respectable performance at the 2016 
Rio Olympic Games. 
 
Indian sportspersons/teams are performing  better a t the international level as compared to 
similar earlier events held in the Olympic discipli nes like Archery, Athletics, Badminton, Boxing, 
Hockey, Shooting, Tennis and Wrestling.  Accordingl y, maximum financial assistance is being 
extended to these disciplines to target and win more medals in future international events. 
 
The qualifications for the 2016 Rio Olympic Games b egan last year (2014) and 
qualification process for various sports discipline s will go on  up to June/July, 2016 depending 

upon schedule and criteria laid down by the Interna tional Sports Federations of the respective 
sports discipline in consultation with the International Olympic Committee (IOC).   
 
Following quota places have been attained by the In dian Sportspersons/teams for participation 
in Rio Olympics 2016, as on 18.9.2015:-  
• Archery - 04  
• Athletics - 07  
• Shooting - 08  
• Hockey – 16 (Men team)  
• Hockey – 16 (Women Team)  
• Wrestling - 01  
 
Annual Calendar for Training and Competitions, (ACT Cs) focusing on preparations for the 
2016 Rio Olympic Games for all identified sports di sciplines have been finalised  and adequate 
budget provisions have been made to support the spo rtspersons, as projected by the concerned 
National Sports Federation (NSF).  
 
Furthermore, in order to supplement the efforts and  to cater the individual needs of the 
identified sportspersons for the 2016 Rio Olympic G ames, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports has 
launched a new scheme ‘Target Olympic Podium’ (TOP) . Under this scheme specific requirement 
of sportspersons i.e. assistance towards individual tailor-made programme is provided.    
 
SPORTS UNIVERSITY IN NORTH-EAST  
 
 
PROMOTION OF SPORTS AMONG DISABLED  
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
53.  The Committee has also gathered that the Paralympics Committee of India (PCI), owing to 
lackadaisical attitude and apathy towards its athle tes, has been suspended by the International 
Paralympics Committee (IPC).  The Committee also sh ows its concern for chaotic condition 
prevailing in PCI for several years mostly due to i ndividual conflicts and proper management, etc.  
    
Action Taken  
 
The Ministry suspended the recognition of Paralympi c Committee of India (PCI) on 22 
nd  
April 2015 till further orders. The decision to sus pend was taken in the wake of numerous serious 
complaints about poor management / conduct of the 1 5 th  National Para Athletics Championships, 
2015 held from 20th -22nd March, 2015 in Ghaziabad (U.P.) in all aspects viz. logistics, technical, 
administrative, etc. An enquiry conducted by Sports  Authority of India (SAI) has found that the 
complaints were largely well-founded. 
PCI has violated the terms and conditions of recogn ition as well as provisions of its own 
constitution. The Government has further noted that  PCI has not been functioning in the best 
interest of Para sport for which it was granted rec ognition as there has been large scale 
dissatisfaction among players and other stakeholder s thus resulting in adverse impact on both the 

development of the sport as well as future opportun ities and prospects of Para athletes in the 
country. The Ministry had earlier issued a ‘Show-cause’ notice to PCI on the subject. 
The International Paralympic Committee (the interna tional body responsible for promotion 
of sports among para athletes to which PCI is affiliated) has suspended PCI for unlimited period of 
time. 
After suspension of Paralympic Committee of India ( PCI) by the International Paralympic 
Committee and the Ministry of Youth Affair and Spor ts,  the Ministry has decided that all the 
matters relating to Para-athletes including selection of athletes for various sporting events, conduct  
of coaching camps, and submission of entries of par a-athletes in international tournaments shall be 
taken care of by Sports Authority of India till further orders.

Recommendations/observations 
 
55.  However, the Committee is surprised to find that Rs . 10 crore was allocated in BE 2014-
15  and it got reduced to Rs. 0.35 crore in RE stag e of year 2014-15 owing to receipt of less 
number of viable names. The Committee hopes that th is scheme of the Department will achieve 
the desired result in the current fiscal for what it has been meant for.    
 
Action Taken  
Budgetary allocation of Rs. 5.00 crore has been mad e during the current financial year for 
the scheme of Human Resource Development in Sports. The Ministry is hopeful that the budgetary 
allocation will be utilized for achievement of objectives of the Scheme.

Recommendations/observations 
 
61.  The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Departm ent will become functional during 
the current fiscal.

early date of the Expenditure Finance Committee (EF C) Meeting. The meeting was scheduled on 
31.03.2015, subsequently postponed, and finally hel d on 04.06.2015. The scheme is being pursued 
on top priority.

ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS  
 
Recommendations/observations  

27.  The Committee finds it very disheartening on the is sue of non-compliance of the 
guidelines of the Department by the NSFs and recomm ends to evolve a suitable mechanism in this 
regard so that the preparation as well as participa tion of the sportspersons in important national 
and international events is not affected adversely. 
 
Action Taken 
 
NSFs are responsible and accountable for the overal l management, direction, control, 
regulation, promotion and development of the discip lines for which they are recognized by the 
concerned International Federations. They are expec ted to discharge these responsibilities in 
consonance with the principles laid down in the Oly mpic Charter or in the charter of the Indian 
Olympic Association or of the relevant Internationa l Federation as the case may be while being 
compliant with Government guidelines applicable to NSFs. In case of non-compliance, where any 
NSF has been suspended/de-recognised, the assistanc e as admissible is given to athletes to 
facilitate their participation in various events by  the Sports Authority of India.  National Sports 
Code is expected to provide for more specific guide lines to be followed by various sports 
federations. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
  
When National Sports Federations (NSFs) are suspend ed/derecognised on account of 
non-compliance of guidelines of the Department, it is the sportspersons who get affected the 
most. At a time when medal prospects in many intern ational events including Olympics, are 
increasing, it is unfortunate to know that these bo dies are not doing their part in promotion 
and development of sports. The extent to which the performance of sportspersons have been 
affected despite the assistance extended by SAI, th e Committee feels, is the looming spectre  
about which the information has not been provided.  The Committee would appreciate if 
concerted efforts are initiated to ensure that thes e problems are tackled earnestly and the 
excuses  for the fillip in the name of National Sports Code is unacceptable.  
 
URBAN SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
35.  The Committee came to know that Rs.40 crores was al located for the purpose in BE 2014-
15 and it was reduced to Rs.25 crores in RE 2014-15 .  The Committee shows its concern that the 
reduction in RE was on account of non-receipt of Ut ilisation Certificates by the implementing 
agencies.  The actual expenditure is amounting to R s. 23.14 crores till February 2015.  The 
Committee finds this as a very good scheme which is  for providing sports infrastructure in urban 
areas.  But the allocation and expenditure pattern in respect of this Scheme has been very 
discouraging.  Rs. 40 crores BE is reduced to Rs. 2 5 crores RE and even that could not be utilized 
fully.  It was perhaps on account of such a poor pa ttern that the allocation for BE 2015-16 has also 
been reduced to Rs. 25 crores.  The Committee, acco rdingly recommends that Department should 
take initiatives to expedite the submission of util ization certificates by the implementing agencies 
in time so that the allocation pattern is not affected adversely in future. 
 
Action Taken 

 
In deference to the wishes of the Committee, it is proposed to take up the matter with the 
Chief Secretaries/ LGs of the States/UTs at the lev el of Secretary (Sports) to expedite the 
Utilization Certificates on priority so as to ensure release of further grants by the department under  
its various schemes. A list of defaulting States/UTs as on 28.05.2015 is attached as Annexure –II.

Non-submission of Utilisation Certificates by the i mplementing agencies seems to be a 
perennial problem where the Department of Sports ha ve failed to win over and get the same 
liquidated within required time. The Department of Sports should take up this matter on 
priority basis so that the implementation of this scheme does not get affected. The Committee 
finds it alarming that the initiatives undertaken b y the Department are not forthcoming in 
streamlining the three vital components viz. alloca tion of funds, execution of work and 
procurement of UCs.  The Committee can only recomme nd that the Department of Sports 
should explore additional viable mechanism so that at least the allocated budget should be 
utilized.  
 
RAJIV GANDHI KHEL ABHIYAN (RGKA)  
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
42. Secondly, this Scheme has to work in convergence wi th different other schemes 
implemented by different Ministries, the Committee feels that there may be possibility of lack of 
adequate co-ordination and synergy in pooling the r esources and the efforts for implementing this 
Scheme effectively. The committee, therefore, is of  the view that a coordination mechanism 
especially for this scheme should be put in place to obviate any such possibility.      
 
Action Taken 
 
In addition to zero allocation of funds at RE stage  for creation of infrastructure under 
RGKA from the inception of the scheme, the scheme w as unable to fetch any money from 
Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DO NER) as the entire allocation of Rs.72 
crore under Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) was made to another department 
and the requirement of RGKA of Rs.90 crore sought f rom the Ministry of Finance was not met. 
The funds expected from Ministry of Panchayati Raj under their scheme of BRGF stands 
transferred to the States. The role of NITI Ayog in allocation of funds under the Additional Central 
Assistance (ACA) Scheme for the Left Wing Extremism  (LWE) affected districts has also ceased. 
The funds available for material component under the MGNREGA Scheme are stated to have been 
fully committed for works under the Swachh Bharat Mission. 
 In view of the changed circumstances for receipt o f funds from various schemes as listed 
above, it is doubtful that the RGKA Scheme will be able to meet its targets, as envisaged in the

longer available to the RGKA. Putting in place a co ordination mechanism as suggested by the 

Committee may not be of much help, as the Ministry of Rural Development may have its own 
priorities and targets to achieve. The other source s of funding have already dried up and the only 
source which can help in achieving the targets is t he adequate allocation of funds by the Ministry 
of Finance.

It is a pitiable situation indeed, that enough funds are not available for promoting and 
developing sports talents in rural areas. As it has  been pointed out, the only source of funds 
for this scheme can come from the Ministry of Finan ce, the Committee is of the view that 
extensive efforts  are required to be made by the D epartment to pursue this matter with the 
Ministry of Finance.  
 
 
  

Recommendations/observations  
 
43.  Thirdly, the Committee is intrigued to note that Rs . 200 crore in the Plan allocation for 
RGKA during BE 2014-15 was reduced to Rs. 85 crores  in RE and even the reduced allocation

implementing agencies.  The Committee finds this di sheartening.  Interestingly, in BE 2015-16,

Rs.95 crores.  The Committee fails to understand with this meagre allocation how the objectives of 
the Department are going to achieved in time.  We h ave more than 50% reduced allocation for this 
Scheme and we are not able to spend even the highly  reduced allocation that too on technical 
procedural grounds as UCs.  The Committee finds that if this is the state of affairs in respect of this 
Scheme then future of this scheme remains highly bl eak.  The Committee, therefore, recommends 
the Ministry to make all out efforts to implement t his scheme with the required zeal and 
dedication.

15 was reduced to Rs.85 crore at RE stage, it appea rs that the drastic reduction in funds to RGKA

proportionately was on account of non-commitment by  the State/UT Governments that they will 
develop the playfield out of funds earmarked under MGNREGA Scheme, which is a pre-requisite

Rural Development to Department of Sports. The othe r reason for not spending the allotted funds 
proportionately before the RE stage was that though  the Department of Sports had received 
proposals for release of funds for organizing vario us competitions at Block, District, State and 
National Levels, much of the same could not be rele ased for want of Utilization Certificates from 
the respective State/UT, which is mandatory as per provisions of General Financial Rules (GFR) 
and the instructions issued by the Ministry of Fina nce. It may thus be seen that the drastic 
reduction in funds to RGKA happened because of reas ons beyond the control of Department of 
Sports. 
 
 As regards observation of the Committee that even the reduced allocation of Rs. 85 crore 
could not be utilized fully, it is submitted that D epartment of Sports had released grants of Rs. 
83.84 crore during 2014-15 and the remaining amount  of Rs. 1.16 crore could not be utilized 
because of the restrictions imposed by the Ministry  of Finance during the last month of the 
financial year. The constraints in achieving the ta rgets have been brought out in the reply to para 
42 of the report. Department of Sports  will make a ll out efforts to implement the scheme with the 
desired zeal and dedication provided funds as proje cted in the scheme documents are made 
available and the constraints are remedied by way of re-visiting the scheme. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
  
 The Committee is unhappy to note that there have b een many reasons for the 
reduction of funds upon which the Department has no  control what so ever.  But this issue of

Department look for alternative means available to them to tackle all these hurdles. The 

Committee impress upon the Department of Sports to take up the matter with the Central

GROSS ENROLMENT RATIO (GER) 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
3.4 Committee’s attention has been drawn by the Twe lfth Plan Approach Paper which 
mentions that about 18 per cent of all Government e ducation spending or 1.12 per cent of GDP be 
spent on higher education. This funding should be r aised to 25 per cent and 1.5 per cent 
respectively. However, the overall scenario regardi ng the declining allocations over the years as 
discussed in preceding paras shows altogether a dif ferent picture. This is also reflected in low 
achievement of GER which is taken as an indicator o f the growth and development of Higher 
Education Sector in the country. As may be seen fro m the comparative figures, India ranks at the 
bottom regarding GER amongst those nations. The Com mittee, therefore, reiterates that to achieve 
higher GER and for making India an educational hub globally, not only more allocations are 
required but the utilization of allocations also has to be more efficient. 
Action Taken 
 
National Policy on Education, 1986 (modified in 199 2) stipulates that investment in 
education should be gradually increased so as to re ach a level of expenditure of 6% of National 
Income as early as possible. The Plan allocation fo r Education shows that there has been a 
phenomenal increase in the Plan Allocation during XI Plan vis-vis X Plan. As against a total actual 
expenditure of Rs. 58817.33 crore (for both the Dep artments) during X Plan, the actual allocation 
for the Ministry of HRD during XI Plan has gone up to Rs. 193570 crore, which is an increase of 
3.3 times. Central XII Plan out of Ministry of HRD have also been increased vis-à-vis XI Plan 
Actual Expenditure of Rs. 1.78 lakh crore (for both  the Department) during XI Plan, the Central 
Plan Outlay of Education during XII Plan has gone u pto 4.54 lakh crore, which is an increase of 
2.55 times. With the several initiatives taken by t he Central Government in the recent past, it is 
expected that expenditure in Education Sector will be faster and the State Government will also 
come forward for investing in Education Sector, as the 6% of GDP has to come from Central as 
well as State Government. About 18 percent of all g overnment education spending or about 1.12 
percentage of GDP is spent on higher education today.  

RASHTRIYA UCHATAR SHIKSHA ABHIYAN (RUSA) 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
4.5 The Committee appreciated the launching of the RUSA and hopes that the objectives of the 
Scheme to help the State Universities and colleges to upgrade themselves both in terms of 
academics and physical infrastructure would go a lo ng way in improving the standard of Higher 
Education in the country. The Committee, however, expresses its concern over declining allocation 
and reduction at RE stage to this scheme since its inception as well as under-utilization. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that this scheme m ay be implemented more efficiently and 
enhanced allocations may be made for achieving desired results. 
Action Taken 
 
(RUSA) 
 -  Funding to states under RUSA is made on the basis of critical appraisal of State Higher 
Education Plans (SHEPs). These plans describe each state’s strategy to address issues of equity, 
access and excellence in higher education. Institut ions are required to prepare “Institutional 
Development Plans” (IDP). These IDPs are then aggre gated to form a SHEP. All funding under 
the RUSA is norm based and future grants are outcom e dependent.  Certain academic, 
administrative and governance reforms are a precond ition for states to receive funding under 
RUSA. The prerequisites include Creation of a State  Higher Education Council, Preparation of 
State Higher Education Plan, State funding commitme nt – share and timeliness, Filling faculty 
positions, Academic and Examination reforms, Governance and administrative reforms, Affiliation 
reforms etc. RUSA fund release is linked to willingness to implement these reforms.  
RUSA implementation started with centre: state shar ing pattern of 65:35 for general category 
states and 90:10 for special category states (North -Eastern States, Sikkim, J&K, Himachal Pradesh 
and Uttarakhand) & UTs. The Central funding in Gene ral Category States has been modified to 
60:40 and to 100% for UTs. This has also led to some delay in release of funds.  
The total funds allocated and released under RUSA, with the approval of the Project Approval 
Board is Rs. 6540.86 Crore and Rs. 820.81 Crore res pectively . The amount approved by the PAB 
has not been released in total on account of the fa ct that the fund released is in instalment and that  
approval to States and UTs in some components are c onditional (e.g. requiring submission of 
complete DPRs, enactment of University Act etc.).  

The BE during the financial year 2015-2016 is Rs.11 55 Crores and funds to the extent of 43% of 
BE have already been released this year as on 30 th  November, 2015.  States have started 
submitting proposals under the entire gamut of comp onents of RUSA. These are being considered 
expeditiously by the PAB.  It is expected that the BE will be fully utilized this year.

IITs 
Recommendations/Observations 
6.16 The Committee observes that the country has do ne extremely well in the field of 
Information Technology, which has become an importa nt tool in the development of manpower 

for various areas of knowledge. The Indian Informat ion Technology manpower has emerged as a 
strong and credible force which is now highly accla imed by the global information 
technology/services industry. The Committee underst ands that in order to provide manpower of 
global standards in the information technology to c ater to the needs of emerging areas of 
knowledge and services, such premier institutes in information technology are an essential pre-
requisite. There is also no denying the fact that t he IT sector has a positive impact on our economy 
and governance which in turn has improved immensely  every aspect of our society, be it 
education, health facilities, agricultural innovati ons or service sector. The Committee welcomes 
the objective behind the proposed institutions but feels concerned about certain visible gaps 
noticed in respect of the status of existing centrally funded IIITs, mode of setting up the new IIITs,  
their governance structure and likely impact on all  the stakeholders that needs to be corrected 
urgently. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The four Centrally Funded IIITs , namely, IIT Allah abad, IIIT&M Gwalior, IIIT D &M 
Kancheepuram and IIIT D&M Jabalpur have been brough t under the ambit of IIIT Act, 2014 
which came into effect from, 5.1.2015. Through this  Act, these 04 CFIIITs have been declared as 
Institutes of National importance.   
As per the IIIT Act, 2014, the following shall be t he authorities of the Institutes :- (i)Board of 
Governors (ii) Senate (iii) Finance Committee (iv) Building & Works Committee (v) Research 
Council and (vi) such authorities as may be declared by the Statutes . 
The Board of Governors of each Institute shall be the Principal executive body of the Institute. 
New IIITs-PPP 
 :- The Scheme of Setting up 20  IIITs in Not for P rofit Public-Private-Partnership 
Mode (N-PPP) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 7 .12.2010. As on date approvals have been 
given for setting up of 19 new IIITs in PPP Mode.  12 IIITs have become functional with the 
commencement of Academic Session in 05 IIITs in 2013-14 ; in 03 IIITs in 2014-15 and in 5 IIITs 
in 2015-16 .  IIITs-PPP are registered as Societies  and are governed by a Memorandum of 
Associations and Rules of the IIIT Society.  The Au thorities of the Institute are the Board of 
Governors, Chairperson of the BoG, Director of the Institute,  Senate , Research Council, Finance 
Committee ,Registrar of the Institute  and such aut horities as appointed or nominated by the Board 
. 

The Board is to generally pursue and carry out the objects of the Society as set forth in the MoA 
and in doing so shall follow and implement the poli cy directions and guidelines laid down by the 
Government of India.  
The Board exercises all administrative and financia l powers of the Society including those vested 
or conferred on it by or under any statute subject,  nevertheless in respect of expenditure, to such 
limitations as the Central Government, from time to time, impose.  
There are ample representation of Industry Partners , State Government and Central Government 
on the BoGs of IIITs -PPP.  
 
FACULTY POSITION 
  
Recommendations/Observations 
 
7.13 The Committee would like to have an evaluation  report, if any, about the quality and 
standard of Ph.D holders across the country to unde rstand why suitable candidates are difficult to 
find for the vacant positions. May be we need to re orient the entire system of evaluation of Ph.D 
and other research scholars. 
 
Action Taken 
 
While no dedicated study for assessing the quality of Ph.D research in the Country has 
been undertaken, as informed by the University Gran ts Commission (UGC), the UGC Review 
Committee constituted by the Central Government in July, 2014 has observed that there is a 
Mushroom growth of sub-standard Ph.D degrees.  The report of the Committee further observed 
that the race for obtaining Ph.D degree has now bec ome a necessity in view of the minimum 
qualification for recruitment at entry level and requirements for promotion.   
In order to serve national purpose of maintaining s tandards of Higher Education and to bring 
uniformity in the procedure of award of M.Phil. / Ph.D. Degree, UGC has framed UGC (Minimum 
Standard and Procedure for the awards of M.Phil/Ph. D. Degree), Regulation 2009. These 
Regulations have been notified in the Gazette of In dia dated 11th-17th July, 2009 and are 
available at UGC website 
www.ugc.ac.in  .  The UGC has written, on 6 th  July, 2015, to the Vice-
Chancellors of all Universities that it has come to the notice of the UGC that some Universities are 
hiring the services of the Supervisors who do not h appen to be the regular teachers of the 
Universities or its affiliated Post Graduate (PG) c olleges/ Institutes awarding the M.Phil/ Ph.D. 

degree. It has observed that this practice is in vi olation of UGC (Minimum standards and 
procedure for award of M.Phil/Ph.D. Degree) Regulat ions, 2009. The UGC has advised the Vice 
Chancellors that Universities shall allocate the su pervisor from amongst the regular faculty 
members in a department or its affiliated PG Colleg es/ institutes depending on the number of 
students per faculty member, the available speciali zation among the faculty supervisors and the 
research interest of the student. It has been furth er clarified by the UGC that any Ph.D. / M.Phil. 
degree awarded by a University under the supervisio n of a Supervisor who is not a faculty 
member of the University or its affiliated PG Colle ges/ Institutes would be in violation of UGC 
(Minimum standards and procedure for award of M.Phil./ Ph.D.) Regulations, 2009.

SKILL DEVELOPMENT 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
9.2 The Committee appreciated the efforts of the De partment to enhance the skill and 
employability of the youth. The Committee pointed o ut that in order to leverage the demographic 
dividend that India enjoys, we need to ensure that our youth are empowered with right skills to 
meet the challenges of the knowledge based economy.  The Committee recommends that some 
strategies for the skill development like skills re quirement assessment, Diploma Education, lateral 
entry from ITIs to Diploma programmes, Industrial t raining finishing schools and Special 
Manpower Development Programme should be taken up. The Committee points out this area 
should be accorded the highest priority as it will impact our development strategies in other areas 
as well. Skill Development, in fact is not confined  to one Ministry/Department; many of them 
including State Governments and Private Sector woul d be involved. Although we have a separate 
Ministry for coordination in this regard, the Commi ttee hopes that such schemes are implemented 
with proper synergy/coordination without any duplication of efforts/ resources. 
  

Action Taken 
 
The University Grants Commission is implementing th ree schemes namely; Community 
Colleges (CC), B.Voc. degree programme and DeenDaya lUpadhyay KAUSHAL Kendras for 
imparting skill based vocational courses at certifi cate, diploma, advanced diploma degree and 
masters as well as research level. The UGC has fram ed the guidelines for curricular aspects, 
assessment criteria and credit system for skill bas ed vocational system through which road to 
understanding is paved with the clearly prescribed assessment criteria and requirements of skills 
competency for specific certificate, diploma or deg ree level programmes. It is also indicated that 
the skill component of the programmes will be asses sed by the concerned sector skills council and 
the same will be certified for being qualified if f ound fit towards skills abilities this will lead to

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
2.5 The Committee observes that there is a huge gap  between the projected demands and actual 
allocations during the Twelfth Plan period i.e. 201 2-17, and with only two years left, it would not 
be possible to cover this gap. Moreover, the reduce d allocation of funds does not match with the 
objectives of Twelfth Plan regarding expansion and growth of Higher Education Sector in the 
Country and that this is also in contrast with the main objective of the improvement of access 
alongwith equity and excellence in Higher Education. The allocation needs to be enhanced. 
Action Taken 
 
The allocation of budget for Central Government Dep artments have been decided by the 
Ministry of Finance on the basis of expenditure tre nd  and the absorptive capacity, existing 
commitments, available fiscal resource position, av ailable fiscal space and demand of various 
Department and sharing pattern between the Central Government and State Government as 
applicable under the schemes.  
Recommendations/Observations 
 
2.8 The Committee, in view of the declining allocat ions combined with underutilization of 
budget allocations, expresses its serious concerns and recommends that the Department should 
reconsider/review its overall mechanism in so far a s the implementation of various schemes is 
concerned and bring in new ideas. This is high time  to show high achievements in the 
growth/development of Higher Education Sector, if I ndia were to compete with advanced 
Countries in this regard. We have to achieve equity , access and excellence in Higher Education to 
overcome the existing inequality prevailing in the Country as well as to bridge the urban/rural 
divide. The Committee, however, also recommends to the Government to take seriously the 
growth and development of this sector and increase budgetary allocations keeping them closer to 
the Twelfth Plan projections made by the Department  of Higher Education as they are serving the 
needs of the society. 

Action Taken 
 
Various schemes and programmes being implemented in  HE Bureau and the UGC are 
constantly reviewed to ensure that the envisaged ou tcomes are achieved along with judicious 
utilization of funds. 
Moreover, the reduction is due to the fact that the re has been a substantial enhancement of direct 
devolution to the State Government. Government of I ndia has rationalized the Scheme provisions 
to ensure that total outlays for the individual schemes do not suffer. 
 
Comments of the Committee (Paras 2.5 & 2.8) 
 
 The Committee does not agree with the reply of the  Department.  The Committee 
feels that Department has not been spending the all ocated amount on the schemes launched 
by them.  The underutilization of the funds allocat ed to the Department has led to 
undermining the projected needs of the Higher Educa tion Sector, leading to decrease in the 
budgetary allocation for the Department.  The Commi ttee recommends that the Department 
should implement the various schemes earnestly.    The Committee also acknowledge that 
now the Government has substantially enhanced the d irect devolution to the state 
governments so that individual schemes do not suffe r on account of funds constraints.  Here 
it becomes imperative upon the Department to active ly pursue with the State Governments 
for proper utilization of funds and periodically ge t the feedback in respect of those schemes.  
Committee would like to apprised of the mechanism h ow the funds are allocated and utilized 
by the mode of direct devolution to the State Gover nments and in what manner the Central

FACULTY POSITION 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
7.11 The Committee has been voicing its concern fro m time to time on the acute shortage of 
faculty in higher educational institutions across t he country. Right from well established Central 
Universities to those set up recently, State univer sities as well as private universities, premier 
institutions like IITs, NITs and IIMs, this problem  has emerged as the biggest handicap for the 
development and growth of Higher Education vis-a-vis  maintaining the quality of education. 
Situation continues to be grim with no improvement foreseen in the near future. The Committee 
points out that the availability of adequate and qu alified faculty is a pre-requisite for quality 

education. The Committee appreciates the steps take n by the Department like increase in the 
retirement age up to 65 years, improvement of salar y structures, etc. The Committee feels that 
there can be only three possibilities, either our y oung students are not attracted towards the 
teaching profession or the recruitment process is a  prolonged involving too many procedural 
formalities or the quality of candidates in not upt o the required level. In either case, the 
Department being the nodal authority for higher edu cation sector has to take a proactive 
role so as to expedite the filling up of the existing vacancies.  
 
Action Taken 
 
In IIMs, the age of retirement of faculty is alread y 65 years. The salary structure of IIMs is 
also one of the best amongst the Government academi c institutions. The quality of education in 
IIMs is one of the best in the country and they con stantly endeavour to keep their quality of 
education and improve it.  
 Keeping in mind the fact that the field of higher education is currently facing an acute shortage of 
teachers at all levels and also being aware of the decision of the central government to expand the 
base of college and university education significan tly throughout the country, the 
UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appoi ntment of Teachers and Other Academic 
Staff in Universities and Colleges and Measures for  the Maintenance of Standard in Higher 
Education, 2010 has extended the age of superannuat ion to 65 years for teachers in University and 
College across the country. 
 Ministry of Human Resource Development and Univers ity Grants Commission have repeatedly 
written to Central Universities to expedite filling  of vacancies of teachers and are continuously 
monitoring the progress. The progress has also been  discussed in the Conference of Vice-
Chancellors of the Central Universities held on 4th  – 5th February, 2015 and Visitor’s Conference 
on 4th -6th November, 2015. Visitor’s nominees have  also been provided to all Central 
Universities for Selection Committees for teachers, to expedite the selection process. 
 
The UGC has allowed the University to re-employ sup erannuated teachers for a maximum 
period of five years, i.e. up to 70 years against s anctioned vacant post, if such posts are not 
filled up by regular candidates. 
Intensive efforts are being made to attract talente d, bright and qualified young men and women to 
college and University jobs. The entry point incent ives have been substantially increased. The 

UGC Regulations, 2010 has prescribed norms for impr ovement in service conditions for the new 
entrant, in terms of better working and leave condi tions, career advancement prospects, retirement 
benefits etc. 
The Central Government has also recommended the con stitution of the UGC pay review 
committee to the Department of Expenditure.  
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
 The Committee has repeatedly been voicing its conc ern on the shortage of faculty in 
higher educational institutions in the country.  Th e Committee notes the re-employment of 
teachers for a period of five years till the age of  70 years as a temporary measure, if such 
posts are not filled up by regular candidates.  The  shortage of faculty in the higher 
educational institutes is also affecting the qualit y of education being imparted in these 
institutions.  The Committee would like to highligh t that this perennial shortage of faculty 
can only be addressed if there is an increase in nu mber of research fellowships and also 
improvement in service condition and increase in re muneration for new entrants.  The 
Committee recommends that the Government needs to take urgent steps to address this issue 
within a definite time frame and also direct the UGC to submit a report on this matter. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
7.12 The Committee also feels that to tackle the sh ortage of faculty in the Higher Educational 
Institutions (HEIs) there should be an increase in the number of research fellowships and new 
schemes for teaching assistantship should be introd uced. The Committee further points out that 
there should be appropriate linkages with S&T insti tutions, joint appointment of teachers and 
researchers as faculty and promotions should be lin ked with performance. The Committee further 
adds that the Department should take steps to enhan ce the prestige of the teaching profession. The 
Committee is also of the view that in case the stri cter norms for the appointment of faculty is 
coming in the way then UGC and other regulatory bod ies should review them on regular basis and 
bring in necessary changes so as to fill up the vacant posts at the earliest. 
Action Taken 
 
 The Government has appointed a Committee on 24 
th  July, 2015, under the Chairpersonship 
of Prof. Arun Nigavekar, former Chairman, Universit y Grants Commission (UGC) to examine the 

issues related to attracting and retaining talented  and quality manpower in the teaching profession.  
The Committee has following members, viz., Shri Sum it Bose, former Secretary, Government of 
India, Prof. Sunil Gupta, former Vice-Chancellor, H imachal Pradesh University, Prof.B. Thimme 
Gowda, Vice-Chancellor, Bangalore University, Prof.  Ashwini Kumar Mohapatra, Professor, 
Jawaharlal Nehru University and Shri S.S.Sandhu, Jo int Secretary, MHRD as Member-Convener. 
The Terms of Reference of the Committee are, namely ; (i) evaluation of the Academic 
Performance Indicator(API) Scheme as regards the en try point and Career Advancement of 
Teachers by taking into account its criticism and s uggest suitable improvements/alternatives, (ii) 
evaluation of Ph.D-NET qualifications for entry of teachers and to accordingly suggest a policy for 
selections and (iii) consideration of the problems and issues related to ad-hoc and contractual 
appointments in Central Universities and recommenda tions to resolve them. The Committee has

The Central Government has also recommended the con stitution of the UGC pay review 
committee to the Department of Expenditure. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 
 The Committee appreciates the appointment of a Com mittee to examine the issues 
related to attracting and retaining talented and qu ality manpower in teaching profession. 
The Committee would further like to point out that attracting and retaining talented people 
to the teaching profession is the key to increase t he quality of education being imparted in 
Higher Education Institutions.  The Committee also appreciates the recommendation of the 
Government for the constitution of the UGC pay revi ew Committee, which is a right step for 
attracting quality manpower to the teaching profess ion.  However, the Committee feels that 
the Government should pursue the matter with the De partment of Expenditure for 
expediting the matter.

 The Committee notes the faculty position as provid ed by the Department.  The

complaint is taken by the SCSC after receipt of the  necessary Action Taken Report (ATR) / reply 
from the concerned bureau and after that necessary approval of competent authority is taken 
accordingly.  As per CVC guidelines anonymous / pse udonymous complaints are not dealt in 
Complaint Cell. 
Grievances relating to UGC and received through the  online grievance redressal portal 
pgportal.gov.in are being monitored rigorously. The  guidelines of the CVC regarding complaints 
related to the UGC are being strictly adhered. To m ake the functioning of the UGC more 
transparent, 16 scholarship schemes have been on bo arded the DBT platform. The UGC is taking 
up e-governance measures to make all its schemes online. 
 
Comments of the Committee (Para 14.2) 
 
 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of t he Department.  The Committee 
points out that UGC, AICTE, NAAC and NAB are regula tory bodies dealing with Higher 
Education in the Country, and there seems to be lac k of transparency in these Institutions, 
Higher Education in suffering in the Country.  The Committee would also like to point out 
that complaint related to these regulatory bodies s hould not just be monitored but action 
should also be taken to address these concerns.  Th e Committee appreciates the online 
redressal portal devised by the UGC and other regul atory bodies like AICTE, etc. should 
adopt such best practices not only for grievances a gainst AICTE approved Institutions but 
those against AICTE itself. 
  

CHAPTER-IV 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
GOVERNMENT ARE STILL AWAITED 
STRENGTHENING OF UGC AND AICTE 
Recommendations/Observations 
13.4 The Committee takes this opportunity to observ e that for quite some time, increasing 
number of students have been opting for technical a nd professional courses for future 
employability thus leaving the fields of social sci ences and humanities neglected. The Committee 
would appreciate if steps are initiated to attract students to the fields of social sciences and 
humanities also as these subjects address vital soc ial issues and public policies. Further, the 
Committee would like the Department to give more fo cus to the three language formula in the 
Education System as it would also strengthen the concept of National integration in our society. 
Action Taken 
An All India Council for Technical Education Review  Committee to restructure and 
strengthen the Technical Education sector was const ituted vide MHRD Note F.No.1-19/2014-TS-
II dated 22.10.2014 and the Committee has since submitted its report to the MHRD in April 2015.  
The comments on the report had been invited from th e stakeholders and the report of the 
Committee is under consideration of the Ministry. 
The Government had constituted a Review Committee h eaded by Dr. Hari Gautam, former 
Chairman, University Grants Commission (UGC) to rev iew the working of the UGC. The 
Committee has submitted its report.  
The report is being examined, in its entirety, in consultation with the Niti Aayog.  
 
Comments of the Committee 
 The Committee wishes that findings of the said two  Committee, and action taken 
thereon be furnished to this Committee.

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
 The Committee does not agree with the reply of the  Department.  The Committee 
feels that Department has not been spending the all ocated amount on the schemes launched 
by them.  The underutilization of the funds allocat ed to the Department has led to 
undermining the projected needs of the Higher Educa tion Sector, leading to decrease in the 
budgetary allocation for the Department.  The Commi ttee recommends that the Department 
should implement the various schemes earnestly.    The Committee also acknowledge that 
now the Government has substantially enhanced the d irect devolution to the state 
governments so that individual schemes do not suffe r on account of funds constraints.  Here 
it becomes imperative upon the Department to active ly pursue with the State Governments 
for proper utilization of funds and periodically ge t the feedback in respect of those schemes.  
Committee would like to apprised of the mechanism h ow the funds are allocated and utilized 
by the mode of direct devolution to the State Gover nments and in what manner the Central

authorities to expedite the process of shifting of IITs to permanent campuses from partially 
shifted condition. The Committee also recommends th at sites for five new IITs announced in

academic section of these institutions and set up their campuses at the earliest.  
                 (Para 6.7)

Comments of the Committee

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
2.9 The Committee finds that the performance of the  Scheme like SABLA has been 
satisfactory, however for the IGMSY Scheme, the phy sical targets remained under-achieved in 
2013-14 and 2014-15.  Schemes related for girl chil d, adolescent girls and women are of vital 
importance, so any problems faced in the achievemen t of targets need to be identified and 
addressed for the efficacious implementation of the schemes.  
Action Taken 
 
The Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana (IGMSY) wa s introduced in 2010-11. A 
baseline survey was conducted by the State Governme nts/UT Administrations at the outset of the 
scheme. The Ministry compiled the number of benefic iaries received from the States/UTs, which 
came out to be 12.5 lakh. The Ministry had undertak en several rounds of review meetings with the 
State Governments/UT Administrations to identify th e reasons for slow pace of implementation of 
scheme. During these interactions, it was realised that some States/UTs have overestimated the 
number of beneficiaries during the baseline survey.  The State Governments/UT Administrations 
were requested to re-estimate the number of benefic iaries which was further reported to be around 
10 lakh annually. For the financial year 2015-16, t he estimated number of beneficiaries remain 
same. The beneficiary coverage reported by the States/UTs has substantially increased from 259 in 
2010-11 to 5.9 lakh and 4.65 lakh in 2013-14 and 20 14-15 (annual reports awaited from 18 
States/UTs) respectively. Performance of the scheme  Sabla has been satisfactory as observed by 
the Committee. Needs no comments. 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
2.12 It has been brought to the attention of the Co mmittee that no internal audit of the Ministry 
has been conducted after 2007.  The Committee is co nstrained to observe that for such an 
important Ministry catering to about 70 per cent of  the population, a systematic and regular 
mechanism for auditing is not put in place.  The Co mmittee would like to point out that internal 
auditing is necessary to add value and improve an o rganization’s operations.  So it is hoped that 
internal auditing is done regularly so that the Ministry can accomplish its objectives.  
 
Action Taken 
 
An O.M. dated 12.06.2015 has been issued to CCA, HR D for conducting Internal Audit of 
this Ministry 
.

VI. BETI  BACHAO BETI PADHAO (BBBP) PROGRAMME 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
6.3   The Committee observes that the steadily decl ining child sex ratio in India has reached 
emergency proportions and urgent action must be tak en to alleviate this crisis. The Committee 
further observes that this decline has taken place despite the best efforts by the Ministry in 
checking this trend. It should be noted that girl c hild is the future of every nation and India is no 
exception.  In a society, both girls and boys, play  equally important roles.  To eliminate girl child 
from the society is a step backward, away from the civilized society.  So, for the society and the 
nation as a whole to grow and progress, the girl ch ild must be saved, cared, nurtured and loved. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Minis try should make all out efforts to check this 
declining CSR in a mission mode and also to put mor e aggressiveness, energy and resources to 
reverse this trend. 
 
Action Taken 
The observation of committee has been noted for compliance.  
 
Under the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) Scheme mul ti-sectoral action in selected 100 
districts (low on CSR) is being carried out to impr ove the declining child sex ratio (0-6 year). In 
addition to above a Nation-wide awareness and advoc acy campaign o change the mindset through 
training sensitization, awareness raising and commu nity mobilization on ground are being carried 
out .

New Adoption guidelines (2015 ) notified by Government of India and upgraded CARING S. w.e.f. 
1st August, 2015. 
 
a. Guidelines Governing Adoption of Children – 2015 
 
Guidelines Governing Adoption of Children -2015 notified on 17th July 2015 and effective 
from 1 
st  August, 2015 recognizes the fact that there is a f amily for every child which means if a 
child is unable to get a family within the country (within the State or in a different State), can be 
placed in inter country adoption as early de-instit utionalization of a child and his/her placement in 
a loving family is paramount. This has replaced the  2011 Adoption Guidelines. The Guidelines 
envisage simplification of adoption procedure and a lso addresses delay in the adoption system. 
Transparency, ethical practices and a strict timeli ne in the adoption process are essentials parts of 
the new Guidelines. There is more emphasis of invol vement of local authority like District Child 

Protection Unit (DCPU) to facilitate adoption etc. Now all recognized adoption agencies will be 
known as Specialized Adoption Agencies and such agencies shall be entitled to place children both 
in-country and inter-country  adoptions. 
 
b. CARINGS (Child Adoption Resource Information & G uidance System): An e-governance 
Initiative 
 
The upgraded IT application has emphasized on e–gov ernance in adoption system - from 
partial online system to complete online system. In  fact, within the country eligible and suitable 
Prospective Adoptive Parents (PAPs) can access prof ile of adoptable children and go for online 
matching. Priority to domestic adoption is ensured through online system. In cases of inter-country 
adoption, once prospective parents are considered e ligible and suitable by CARA, online matching 
is possible through the sponsoring foreign agency o r authority. In cases of all adoptable children, 
relevant information are captured in the CARINGS be ginning from their admission till the child 
gets adoption decree and post adoption follow–up for a period of two years.

X. RASHTRIYA MAHILA KOSH (RMK) 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
10.4  With Andaman and Nicobar Islands as exception , the Committee observes that in 
all the States/UTs, the amount of loan disbursed to  poor women was less than the sanctioned 
amount indicating that funds are lying un-utilized with IMOs in these States.  The Committee is 
dismayed with the findings that in certain States l ike Karnataka and Punjab, less than half of the 
sanctioned amount was being disbursed.  The same si tuation prevails in the UT of Puducherry in 
which funds amounting to only `16 crore is being disbursed since inception against  a sanctioned 
amount of `51 crore.  A major discrepancy observed by the Comm ittee is the number of 
beneficiaries vis-à-vis loans disbursed.  In the St ate of Assam e.g. against `453.90 lakh disbursed, 
there were only 6605 beneficiaries.  The same can b e said for the State of Bihar where `468.83 
lakh benefitted 17,156 women.  The Committee notes this issue and strongly feels that a 
monitoring mechanism should be put in place to curt ail any discrepancy that arises in the whole 

process.  Also, the Committee feels that the fund s anctioned should be duly disbursed without any 
delay as this Scheme aims for the economic empowerment of the poor women. 
Action Taken 
As per loan norms of RMK, Sanctioned loan is disbur sed in two parts. 50% of the 
sanctioned loan is released immediately after sanct ion and execution of necessary loan documents 
by the NGOs. 2nd and last installment of 50% sancti oned loan is released after completion of the 
following formalities:- 
(i)  Submission of required Disbursement certificat e, list of beneficiaries with their 
photographs and signature, and 2nd Drawl applicatio n with appendance to drawal, 
etc. by the loanee NGOs. 
(ii)  Conduction of Post Sanction Study (PSS) by RM K officials other than the 
sanctioning officials. This PSS is usually conducte d after completion of initial 6 
months of moratorium. During this PSS the RMK offic ials see the end use of funds 
released in 1st instalment and after ensuring the s atisfactory utilization of funds 
they recommend for 2nd release. 
Thus it will be observed that it is not the questio n of sanctioned loan funds lying unutilized 
but rather pending compliance of aforesaid conditio ns, that this difference between the sanctioned 
and disbursed amounts happen. 
 
Pointed out state wise position is given below: 
  Punjab :  Against the sanctioned amount of Rs. 141 lacs, r eleased amount is 
Rs 103.50 lacs and not Rs. 37.50 lacs. Reason being  one NGO from Sangrur, Punjab 
namely Bisnouli Sarvodaya Gramodyog Sewa Sansthan a ccount no. 1878 and 1663 was 
sanctioned Rs. 66 lacs and was released 100% itself  in two stages. But during the loan 
period itself this account was transferred from Pun jab state to Delhi consequent upon their 
shifting. Hence amount of Rs. 66 lacs was appearing  in Delhi State. Thus total 
disbursement for Punjab state is Rs. 103.50 (37.50 + 66) lacs and not only Rs. 37.50 lacs as 
given in the table.  
Karnataka :  The major cause of difference between sanctioned  and disbursed 
amount is because of the aforesaid reason given in para (a) above. There seem to be a 
typical mistake. Against the sanction amount of Rs. 51 lacs  and not crore that Rs. 16 lacs is 
disbursed. Hence this amount should be read in lacs  only as the tabular figures are in lacs 
only. For UT Puducherry, the difference between san ctioned and disbursed amount is 
because of the aforesaid reason given in para (a) above. 
 
As regards the observation of Hon‘ble Committee mem bers on the no. of beneficiaries vis-
à-vis loan disbursed, it is submitted that it depen ds upon the kind of activity for which loan is 
sanctioned. From the given figures, arrived at per beneficiary loan amount of Rs. 6,872 for Assam 
state is for purchase of milch animals, silk worm r earing, piggery etc. while in Bihar per 
beneficiary loan amount of Rs. 2,732 is towards goa try, pickle, masala making, etc. Hence there is 
no direct relation between the number of beneficiaries and loan amount. 
 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee takes note of the reply. As regards the non-utilization of sanctioned 
amount, it appears that the respective State Govern ments did not comply to the norms of 

RMK. The Committee is concerned about this aspect a s it appears from the reply of the 
Government that the Ministry is unable to control t his trend. The Committee is constrained 
to observe that such a plea cannot be tenable. The Ministry of Women and Child 
Development has to be proactive in motivating the r espective State Governments to comply 
with the norms of the scheme; ascertain the difficu lties, if any, are being faced by them and 
find the way how the issue of non-utilization of sa nctioned grants can be addressed. If need 
be, the Ministry can also revisit its norms. Furthe r, the Committee fails to understand how 
one NGO from Punjab was permitted to transfer its a ccount to Delhi. The Committee 
believes that the grants are State specific and acc ordingly desires a detailed note on this 
issue.

XVIII.     CONCLUSION 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
18.1 The Ministry of Women and Child Development wa s set up as a nodal agency with the 
prime aim to empower and promote holistic developme nt and welfare of women and children who 
are considered the vulnerable sections of society.  The Ministry has formulated many women and 
child centred legislations, plans, policies and pro grammes to ensure women’s empowerment as 
well as gender equality to the extent possible and to ensure children’s holistic development and 
growth.  The Committee is aware that the Ministry has to cater to more than 70 per cent of the total 

population and that too the most vulnerable ones.  It, therefore, has indeed a massive 
responsibility.  The Committee finds the performanc e of the Ministry satisfactory but still a lot 
more needs to be done, particularly for arresting t he rising crimes against women and children.  
The Committee strongly feels that the Ministry shou ld ensure safety and security to women 
including at the workplace, by ending all forms of discrimination, exploitation, harassment and 
violence against women by strictly implementing the  relevant laws promulgated for the purpose.  
Further, the Ministry should strive towards ensurin g zero tolerance to all kinds of exploitation of 
children including child labour, sexual abuse and v iolence, by providing legislative and 
institutional support. The Committee is of the view  that the Ministry would find it very difficult to 
fulfill the objectives of empowerment of women in a ll walks of life due to massive cut in funds 
this year. The Committee also feels that it should have better coordination with the State 
Governments and various agencies, NGOs for implemen ting women/children centric schemes for 
more better results. 
 
Action Taken 
 
 The Committee’s observations are noted for complia nce. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee takes note of the various efforts ta ken up by the Ministry to handle 
various issues relating to welfare of women and chi ldren. However, the Committee observes 
that the Ministry has failed to provide information  and data on various important schemes 
and the some of the information given are not up to  date. The Ministry has adopted a very 
casual approach while replying on the recommendatio ns of the Committee. Many issues and 
challenges regarding the welfare and protection of women and children are in lurch. It is 
hoped that the Ministry adopt serious and concerted efforts in tackling such problems.  
 The Committee is exasperated to note that out of i ts 35 recommendations contained in 
the report, the Ministry of Women and Child Develop ment has merely “noted for 
compliance” on 18 of those recommendations even tho ugh the financial year is coming to an 
end. No steps/action taken by them has been indicat ed in the ATN. Many of the figures 
provided by the Ministry are not up to date and in some cases, figures for the current 
financial year are missing altogether. These do not  speak well of the Ministry and the casual 
approach being adopted by them in implementing various schemes does not bode well for the 
future of women and children of this country. The C ommittee, therefore, recommends that 
the Ministry should start with a new zeal to ensure  that such a important facet of the society 
i.e., women and child development does not suffer d ue to their apathy and urgent steps 
should be taken seriously for the future of the country. 
 The Ministry was mandated to provide the Action Ta ken Note on the 
recommendations/observations contained in the Repor t within 90 days of the 
presentation/laying of the Report. However, the Com mittee is anguished to note that despite 
several reminders, the same was received quite late . Hence, the Committee recommends that 
the Ministry should strictly adhere to the stipulated timeframe.

and 2013-14. However in the year 2014-15, the funds  have not been utilised to the fullest 
extent, the reason for which has not been given by the Ministry. The Committee appreciates 
the efforts of the Ministry in covering the targete d number of beneficiaries for nutrition 
during 2014-15.  
The Committee is sad to note that implementation of  such an important scheme will 
be affected if enough funds are not allotted. The M inistry has submitted that the States 
would require to put in more money as the budget al location for the year 2015-16 for this 
scheme has been reduced. The experience with States  contributing their share had not been 
very encouraging. Hence, the Committee observes tha t the Ministry should take up this issue 
with the States/UTs earnestly so that the implementation of this scheme does not get affected. 
Also, the Ministry should approach the Ministry of Finance for more allocation of funds. 
                         (Para 2.5) 
 
 
 
 It is unfortunate to note that the Ministry of Fin ance has not allotted any fund for the 
implementation of SAKSHAM. The Ministry has failed to cite any reason why schemes such 
as Restorative Justice for Rape Victims, Women’s he lpline, Assistance for construction of 
shelter home for single women have still not been a pproved for implementation. The 
Committee is of the view that the issue of non-appr oval of the schemes for implementation 
needs to be worked out at the earliest so that the public, at large, are not deprived of the 
benefits of these schemes.                 (Para 2. 7) 
 
 
 
 The Committee is not happy with the way the Minist ry tackles this issue of Utilisation 
Certificates. Latest status of Utilisation Certific ates does not indicate a satisfactory position. 

The Committee would appreciate if proactive efforts  are initiated by the Ministry for 
liquidating the very old Utilisation Certificates. The Committee desires that a detailed status 
report be sent to the Committee. The Committee desi res that the modalities and a status 
report be sent to the Committee. Simultaneously, pe ndency pertaining to the recent years 
also needs to be brought to the minimum level. Cont inuance of pending Utilisation 
Certificates only indicates that the various scheme s meant for the welfare of children and 
women, the most vulnerable sections of the society are not being implemented in a time-
bound manner. The Committee also recommends the Min istry to prepare a timeline to get 
the UCs and take punitive action against defaulting  organizations for non-submission of 
Utilization Certificates.               (Para 2.11)  
 
IV. INTEGRATED CHILD DEVELOPMENT SERVICES SCHEME (I CDS) 
 
 
 The Ministry has claimed that many important activ ities under the ICDS could not be 
taken up due to insufficient funds. The Committee w ould like to point out that the Ministry 
has not taken up this issue earnestly with the Mini stry of Finance nor has the Ministry 
mentioned any back-up plan if the States fail to co ntribute their shares. Instead of exploring 
ways to make this scheme more successful, the Minis try has chosen to give a very 
perfunctory reply. The Committee feels that Ministr y should put in more collaborative 
efforts to see that the State Governments contribut e their share as soon as possible so that 
the projected targets can be achieved efficiently and in a timely manner. The Committee is of 
the view that the outreach of ICDS should be extend ed to every habitation and groups so 
that more women and children benefit from the schem e. The Committee, therefore, 
reiterates that the problem of insufficient funds s hould be dealt with earnestly without any 
delay.                    (Para 4.5) 
 
 
 AWCs are expected to play a vital role in carrying  out the activities under the ICDS 
scheme. However, most of the AWCs lack basic facili ties such as drinking water, toilets etc. 
According to the Ministry, less than fifty per cent  of the AWCs in the country have toilet 
facilities. The Committee would like to point out t hat the Ministry has a long way to go in 
achieving the projected targets. The Ministry has l isted out the hurdles that came in the 
process of providing toilets in AWCs, however, ways  to solve these hurdles have not been 
provided.               (Para 4.13)

 The Committee observes that two years have passed since the scheme was launched, 
yet no achievements have been made so far. The Comm ittee is of the view that the Ministry 
has not taken up this issue seriously. The Committe e strongly feels that the Ministry should 
properly implement this scheme so that the maximum benefits can be derived from this 
scheme.                (Para 4.16) 
 
 
  

Staff and Key Functionaries of ICDS 
 
 The successful implementation of the ICDS scheme s olely depends on its staff. The 
Committee is of the view that all problem areas sho uld be sorted out and pave the way for 
filling up of posts of ICDS functionaries. The Mini stry should take up this matter with the 
concerned State Government at the earliest. The nee d of the hour is to re-vitalise the ICDS 
scheme by filling up of vacant posts without any further delay.                       (Para 4.21) 
 
 The AWWs and AWHs play a very important role in th e proper implementation of 
the ICDS scheme. They perform a myriad of activitie s. It is important that these workers are 
remunerated properly. The Committee takes note of t he efforts undertaken by the 
Government of India in revising the honoraria of AW Ws from time to time. The Committee 
is of the view that paying a sum of only Rs. 2250/-  per month to the workers is quite less as 
compared to the work performed by these AWWs. It is  high time that the Ministry enhance 
the honorarium paid to AWWs as they are the most crucial functionary of the ICDS scheme. 
                (Para 4.24)  
 
 The Committee is disappointed with the way the iss ue of finalising the awards for 
ICDS functionaries is being tackled. The committee is of the view that any award has to be 
announced and given at the earliest. Only then, it can be ensured that the awardees have 
been motivated in the real sense. This fact may be impressed upon the concerned State 
Governments. Procedural constraints leading to undu e delay may be identified and 
corrective steps should be taken accordingly.          (Para 4.26)

 The Ministry should have informed the Committee re garding the plans to take up

XVIII.     CONCLUSION 
 
 The Committee takes note of the various efforts ta ken up by the Ministry to handle 
various issues relating to welfare of women and chi ldren. However, the Committee observes 
that the Ministry has failed to provide information  and data on various important schemes 
and the some of the information given are not up to  date. The Ministry has adopted a very 
casual approach while replying on the recommendatio ns of the Committee. Many issues and 
challenges regarding the welfare and protection of women and children are in lurch. It is 
hoped that the Ministry adopt serious and concerted efforts in tackling such problems.  
 The Committee is exasperated to note that out of i ts 35 recommendations contained in 
the report, the Ministry of Women and Child Develop ment has merely “noted for 
compliance” on 18 of those recommendations even tho ugh the financial year is coming to an 
end. No steps/action taken by them has been indicat ed in the ATN. Many of the figures 
provided by the Ministry are not up to date and in some cases, figures for the current 
financial year are missing altogether. These do not  speak well of the Ministry and the casual 
approach being adopted by them in implementing various schemes does not bode well for the 
future of women and children of this country. The C ommittee, therefore, recommends that 
the Ministry should start with a new zeal to ensure  that such a important facet of the society 
i.e., women and child development does not suffer d ue to their apathy and urgent steps 
should be taken seriously for the future of the country. 
 The Ministry was mandated to provide the Action Ta ken Note on the 
recommendations/observations contained in the Repor t within 90 days of the 
presentation/laying of the Report. However, the Com mittee is anguished to note that despite 
several reminders, the same was received quite late . Hence, the Committee recommends that 
the Ministry should strictly adhere to the stipulated timeframe.                     (Para 18.1)
